items.q: What does ezgmail.unread() return a list of?
options: GmailMessage objects, one for each unread email
GmailThread objects, one for each conversation
Strings holding the subject of each email
rationales: unread(), recent() and search() return threads; the messages are inside each thread's messages list.
The objects have attributes; summary() prints text, but the function returns thread objects.

items.q: smtplib's send_message(msg) is given a message with To, Cc and Bcc fields. What happens to the Bcc addresses?
options: They are sent the message, but the Bcc field is not transmitted
They are ignored, because only To and Cc are recipients
They are sent the message and the Bcc field shows all to everyone
rationales: send_message reads the recipients from To, Cc and Bcc; a blind copy is delivered.
Hiding the Bcc field is the point of a blind copy; send_message does not transmit it.
13 is the number of characters; the limit of 4,096 is counted in bytes.
14 would be right if only one letter were outside ASCII; the word has three letters ı, each of two bytes.

items.q: json.loads(text) is called on the whole text of a poll response that holds two JSON objects on two lines. What happens?
options: It returns a list of two dictionaries
It raises JSONDecodeError (Extra data)
It returns only the dictionary of the first line
rationales: json.loads reads one JSON document; two objects on two lines are not one document, so the text is split into lines first.
It does not stop after the first object; it raises an error about the data that follows.

options: Request(url)
Request(url, headers={'Title': 'Hi'})
Request(url, data=b'Hello, world!')
rationales: Without data the method is GET.
Headers alone do not change the method; it stays GET.

items.q: A sender text is 'al@inventwithpython.com' (no space). What does s[:s.find(' ')] give?
options: 'al@inventwithpython.com'
'al@inventwithpython.co'
'al'
rationales: find returns -1 when there is no space, and the slice [:-1] drops the last character.
That would be the cut at the @ sign; the code cuts at a space.

items.q: The chapter prints str(datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(1797823712)) as '2026-12-20 21:28:32'. Why might your computer print another time?
options: Without a tz argument the result is the clock time of the computer, so the zone matters
fromtimestamp counts from a different epoch on each operating system
The timestamp is in milliseconds and must be divided by 1000 first
rationales: The epoch is the same everywhere; only the conversion to a clock time uses the zone.
The time key of ntfy is in seconds; it is Gmail's internalDate that is in milliseconds.

items.q: A notification n was sent without a title or a priority. What are n.get('title') and n.get('priority', 3)?
options: None and 3
KeyError for both
'' and 0
rationales: Indexing with n['title'] would raise KeyError; get returns a default instead.
get returns None for a missing key unless another default is given, and 3 was given for the priority.

items.q: Since 14 March 2025, what is true of logging in to Gmail with smtplib?
options: The ordinary account password no longer works; OAuth 2.0 (or an app password) does
smtplib can no longer connect to Gmail in any way
Only port 25 is accepted and the password is sent in plain text
rationales: Google's pages list smtp.gmail.com and OAuth 2.0 for standard clients; it is the password login that ended.
Google lists port 465 (SSL) and 587 (TLS) for its SMTP server.

items.q: Which is one of the chapter's disadvantages of an SMS email gateway?
options: The text can only be sent from a Gmail account
The recipient has no way of replying
Every text costs a fee to the sender
rationales: Any email account can mail a gateway address; the gateway belongs to the carrier.
Gateways are described as free; the chapter names fees for telecom APIs such as Twilio instead.

items.q: Why does the command-by-mail program check a password in the message and not the From address?
options: The From address is often empty in mail
The From address is easily faked, so it proves nothing
Passwords are needed because mail is encrypted
rationales: A message normally has a From field; the issue is that its value can be set by anyone.
Encryption is not the reason; the chapter says faking a from address is fairly trivial.
